title: Minnapaugs (Horton's Point Pond)
summary: William Wallace Tooker links Minnapaugs with a small freshwater pond by Long Island Sound at Horton's Point in Southold. The place also appears in Hashamomuk Neck boundary language, tying the pond to a wider named landscape west of Greenport.
history_content: Minnapaugs connects pond geography, wooded island imagery, and the Hashamomuk Neck boundary landscape.
translation_content:
A recorded form is Monnepaught. The name is interpreted as little island pond, combining language for a small island with a water place or pond.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place-names are a unique set of data that expose multiple layers of a language and its speakers.”

— Megan Eichas, Place-Names of Rochester, New York (2020), Abstract, printed p. 93
whereintheworld_content: Tooker describes Minnapaugs as a small pond near Horton's Point in Southold. Coastal pond edges can shift over time, and the precise historic shoreline remains uncertain.
